steps.intent: The United States’ objective is to renew UNISFA’s mandate while embedding clear, measurable benchmarks that hold Sudan and South Sudan accountable for demilitarization, joint institutions, police deployment, visa issuance, and civilian leadership. We also aim to maintain strong language condemning RSF interference and attacks on peacekeepers, while keeping the resolution focused enough to secure at least nine votes and avoid a veto. The main difficulties will be overcoming Russian and Chinese skepticism of benchmark-driven conditionality and resisting attempts by Sudan and South Sudan to weaken language on unauthorized forces and host-government obligations.

messages.Algeria: We thank the United States for the draft and support the renewal of UNISFA. As A3+, we would like the text to preserve host-state consent and avoid making renewal appear conditional on benchmarks that are not matched by adequate resources and consultation. We also seek balanced operative language on South Sudan’s facilitation of UNISFA redeployment, in line with the Status of Forces Agreement. We request further closed consultations before the vote.
messages.China: China supports the renewal of UNISFA’s mandate and appreciates the penholder’s efforts. However, we have serious reservations about linking multiple political benchmarks to the Mission’s future renewal, which risks undermining Council unity and the mission’s stability. We therefore request deletion of OP2 and the related benchmark assessment in OP10, and ask for more balanced language in PP16 that does not attribute lack of progress solely to the parties. China is ready to work constructively toward a text we can support.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the renewal of UNISFA’s mandate and its protection-of-civilians role. We ask that the benchmarks in OP2 be clearly framed around mandate implementation and parties’ cooperation, rather than as automatic criteria for the mission’s future, with progress assessed in the context of Sudan and South Sudan. We also seek strengthened WPS and conflict-related sexual violence reporting in OP10 and the related PP language.
messages.France: France thanks the United States for its penholder role and supports the draft as presented. We welcome its emphasis on UNISFA's mandate, the withdrawal of unauthorized forces, accountability for attacks on UN personnel, and unimpeded humanitarian access. France encourages all parties to implement fully the 2011 Agreement and calls for the protection of civilians, including women and children, in Abyei. We will vote in favour.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the renewal of UNISFA and the balanced text before us. We would ask the penholder to strengthen the protection and accountability language for civilians and humanitarian personnel, and to make the humanitarian access call more explicit and sustained. We can support the draft with these adjustments.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the renewal of UNISFA, but we remain concerned that the draft conditions future renewal on unrealistic benchmarks that could jeopardize the Mission’s preservation. We request that OP2 make clear that any decision on UNISFA’s future remains with the Council and that the listed efforts are indicative, not preconditions. We also ask that the September 2026 deadline be removed or softened to “as soon as possible” to avoid setting the Mission up for failure.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports renewal of UNISFA's mandate and appreciates the penholder's efforts, but we cannot accept language that conditions the Mission's future renewal on political benchmarks to be fulfilled by Sudan and South Sudan. As a major troop-contributor, we ask that paragraph 2 be reframed as political-track objectives, explicitly without prejudice to renewal, and that paragraph 10's reporting requirement be aligned accordingly. We remain ready to support the text once this decoupling is reflected.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the renewal of UNISFA and appreciates the penholder’s balanced text. We request the reinsertion of previously agreed language on climate change as a threat multiplier and on conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence, as their removal weakens the Council’s response to the compounded risks in Abyei. We also ask that the benchmarks in OP2 be framed as indicative, reasonable and realistic—not an automatic precondition—and developed in consultation with Sudan, South Sudan, troop- and police-contributing countries and affected stakeholders.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the renewal of UNISFA’s mandate and commends the United States for the balanced text. We would welcome two additions: an explicit call for all parties to comply with international humanitarian law and ensure accountability for violations, and a reference to preventing and responding to sexual and gender-based violence in Abyei, consistent with the Women, Peace and Security agenda.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation cannot accept the repetition of resolution 2802’s flawed premise. UNISFA’s presence must not be conditioned on political benchmarks or withdrawal scenarios; peacekeepers are deployed to fill a security vacuum and protect civilians. We therefore ask the penholder to delete OP2 and the benchmark-based assessment in OP10, and to avoid accusatory language against the host governments. With these changes we could support the renewal.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone thanks the United States for the balanced draft and supports the extension of UNISFA's mandate. We propose three targeted amendments: explicit reference to famine risk in the Abyei Area, recognition of the African Union and IGAD's role, and ensuring that any withdrawal of unauthorized forces is coordinated with UNISFA to avoid a security vacuum. We remain flexible and ready to work with the penholder.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the renewal of UNISFA and thanks the United States for its efforts. We ask for more explicit language on climate change and on sexual and gender-based violence prevention and response, consistent with the concerns we have raised. Concretely, we propose amendments to PP19, a new operational paragraph after OP9, and an addition to the reporting request in OP10. We remain flexible but consider these changes important.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the renewal of the UNISFA mandate and the balanced approach in the draft. We welcome the focus on demilitarization, humanitarian access, and protection of civilians. We have no changes to request at this stage and encourage the Council to adopt the text promptly.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports renewal of UNISFA's mandate and the text's strong demands on the parties. We ask the penholder to restore explicit climate-security language and to strengthen the humanitarian and WPS provisions so that the specific needs of women and girls, including survivors of conflict-related sexual violence, are addressed. We can support the draft with those targeted additions.

steps.summary: The revision preserves UNISFA renewal and benchmark reporting while clarifying that benchmarks are indicative and not an automatic precondition, and removes the fixed assessment date. It also broadens protection, humanitarian, WPS, climate and host-accountability language to build Council support. The United States expects broad adoption, with China and Russia likely abstaining over residual benchmark concerns.

messages.Algeria: Algeria welcomes the penholder’s partial acceptance of our earlier proposals, particularly the softened benchmarks and conditions-based language. To fully meet A3+ concerns, we still need OP3 to refer explicitly to close consultation with the host Governments, troop- and police-contributing countries, and the African Union and IGAD, not merely taking their views into account. With those adjustments, Algeria is prepared to support the text.
messages.China: China thanks the penholder for the partial acceptance of our earlier concerns, including the clarification that the paragraph 2 list is indicative and non-automatic. We can support the text if the remaining concerns on OP2 are addressed. Specifically, OP2 should be recast as indicative steps rather than 'demonstrable progress' benchmarks, and OP3 should state clearly that these steps are not conditions for UNISFA’s renewal, drawdown or adjustment. We also suggest deleting OP2(e), which concerns mission configuration rather than host-State cooperation.
messages.Denmark: Denmark thanks the penholder for incorporating our priorities on the benchmark language and on Women, Peace and Security, conflict-related sexual violence, and context-sensitive reporting. The current text preserves UNISFA’s protection-of-civilians mandate and ensures that benchmarks are not treated as automatic preconditions for renewal. Denmark supports the draft and is ready to vote in favour.
messages.France: France fully supports the draft and thanks the United States for its efforts. We welcome the extension of UNISFA’s mandate and the strengthened language on protection of civilians, humanitarian access, accountability, and the role of women in peace processes. France calls on Sudan and South Sudan to cooperate fully with UNISFA and to comply with the 2011 Agreement. We urge all Council members to support the text.
messages.Greece: Greece welcomes revision 1 and the incorporation of our proposals on the protection of civilians, accountability, and sustained humanitarian access. The text is balanced, mandate-focused, and consistent with Greece's support for UNISFA and the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Sudan and South Sudan. Greece supports adoption of the draft as it stands and encourages the Council to speak with one voice.
messages.Guyana: The A3+ thanks the penholder for reflecting our core concerns: OP2 is now clearly indicative, OP3 preserves the Council’s authority and rules out automatic preconditions, and the September 2026 deadline has been softened to “as soon as possible”. On that basis, Guyana can support the current text. We continue to stress that UNISFA’s renewal must not be made contingent on unrealistic benchmarks and that the mission must be preserved.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan thanks the penholder for reflecting our core concern in OP3 by clarifying that the benchmarks are indicative and do not constitute an automatic precondition for UNISFA’s renewal, and that the views of troop- and police-contributing countries will be taken into account. As a major troop contributor, Pakistan supports the renewal of UNISFA’s mandate and the current text. We will continue to stress that the mission’s future must be performance-based and not contingent on external political benchmarks beyond its control.
messages.Panama: Panama thanks the penholder for incorporating our concerns on conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence, climate-related security risks, and the indicative nature of benchmarks. To finalize our support, we ask that OP2 make clear that the benchmarks are reasonable and realistic and were developed in close consultation with Sudan, South Sudan, troop- and police-contributing countries and relevant stakeholders. This would ensure that benchmarks remain a constructive tool and do not become rigid preconditions, consistent with our long-standing position. With that adjustment, Panama can vote in favour of the text.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea thanks the penholder for incorporating our language on international humanitarian law accountability and sexual and gender-based violence. We support the current text and encourage the Council to proceed to adoption without further delay, given the urgent need to renew UNISFA and address the deteriorating situation in Abyei.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation appreciates the removal of the fixed assessment and the neutralization of visa language, but OP2 still creates a benchmark-based linkage that we cannot accept. We insist on replacing OP2 with a simple call for full cooperation with UNISFA and compliance with the 2011 Agreement, and on removing the consequential benchmark references in OP3. We also ask the penholder to drop the 'threat multiplier' and climate-related security reporting language, which falls outside UNISFA's mandate and distracts from the security and humanitarian tasks at hand. If these concerns are not addressed, we will abstain.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone thanks the penholder for incorporating our proposals on the African Union and IGAD, the confirmation of famine conditions and risk of famine, and UNISFA-coordinated withdrawal language. We support the current text and call for its adoption. We urge Sudan and South Sudan to cooperate fully with UNISFA, ensure unhindered humanitarian access, and protect civilians and peacekeepers.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the revised draft and thanks the penholder for incorporating climate-related risk language and operational provisions on the prevention of and response to sexual and gender-based violence, including in reporting. We believe the text preserves UNISFA's stabilizing role and the conditions-based approach to any future mandate adjustment. Slovenia is ready to vote in favour.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the revised draft as presented. We welcome the recognition of the African Union and IGAD, the emphasis on humanitarian access, climate-related security risks, and women’s participation, and the confirmation that benchmarks are indicative rather than automatic preconditions for UNISFA’s renewal. Somalia has no further changes to request and encourages the Council to move toward adoption.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom welcomes the revised text, including the climate-security, WPS and vulnerable groups language, and thanks the United States for incorporating our earlier requests. We can support the draft, but we ask for one further addition to OP3: that any decision on UNISFA's future explicitly take into account the implications for the protection of civilians. This is essential to ensure that mandate adjustments remain conditions-based and do not undermine UNISFA's ability to protect civilians.

replies.Russian Federation: rejected: OP2 benchmarks and climate-security language retained.
replies.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: accepted: OP3 now references implications for protection of civilians.

steps.summary: The revision accepts Algeria, Panama and UK requests, retains the US benchmark framework with additional clarification, and rejects Russia's call to delete benchmarks and climate language. It is expected to be adopted with 13 votes in favour and 2 abstentions (China, Russia).

reasons.Algeria: Algeria’s requested changes on AU/IGAD consultation and conditions-based adjustments were accepted, and supporting the renewal aligns with its consistent support for UNISFA and African-led consultation. Though it sought prior closed consultations, the text now addresses its key concerns.
reasons.China: The draft still retains the benchmark framing that China identified as a red line, despite limited clarification in OP3. Consistent with its prior abstention on resolution 2802 and its support for UNISFA’s renewal, China abstains rather than vetoes.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark supports UNISFA’s essential role and the draft’s strengthened language on WPS, climate-related risks, and non-automatic benchmarks. Denmark had no outstanding requests and voted in favour of the prior UNISFA resolution.
reasons.France: France supports renewing UNISFA and has consistently voted in favour of Council texts on Abyei and Sudan; the draft aligns with French priorities on civilian protection, humanitarian access, and accountability. There is no reason for France to oppose or abstain.
reasons.Greece: Greece fully supported the draft without requests and has consistently voted in favour of renewing UNISFA. A supportive explanation of vote is consistent with Greece’s emphasis on international law, protection of civilians, humanitarian access and cooperation with UN peacekeeping.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana has consistently supported UNISFA renewals and voted for resolution 2802 despite concerns; this draft incorporates paragraph 3 limiting benchmarks as automatic preconditions, aligning with A3+ requests. Guyana would likely speak in favour on behalf of the A3+ before the vote.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan’s core concern was that benchmarks not be made automatic preconditions for UNISFA renewal; the revised draft explicitly addresses this in OP3. With that concern accommodated, Pakistan supports renewal and votes yes.
reasons.Panama: Panama has consistently supported UNISFA renewals and its key requested amendment on benchmarks was accepted, along with climate and SGBV language it has championed.
reasons.Republic of Korea: Republic of Korea has consistently supported UNISFA renewals and the protection of civilians in Abyei, and the draft aligns with its stated priorities on peacekeeping, humanitarian access, accountability, and a conditions-based approach. No ROK concerns required abstention or a negative vote.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia has consistently abstained on Abyei mandate renewals with objectionable benchmarks while supporting UNISFA’s continuation, as shown by its abstention on resolution 2802 just before. The current draft, though slightly softened by OP3, still retains the rejected OP2 benchmarks and climate language, so abstention remains the realistic stance rather than a veto.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supported the draft in the final negotiation round and has consistently voted in favour of UNISFA renewal resolutions; there is no record or indication that it would speak before the vote.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia has consistently supported UNISFA’s renewal and the draft incorporates key climate, gender and protection language while preserving conditions-based benchmarks. This aligns with Slovenia’s earlier vote and stated concerns.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia has consistently supported renewal and stabilization mandates on this file and aligns with AU/IGAD coordination, protection of civilians, and conditions-based benchmarks. Its prior vote in favour of resolution 2802 and stated support in the last round make a yes vote the most consistent position.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports renewing UNISFA’s mandate, and its requested OP3 language on protection-of-civilians implications was accepted, so it will vote in favour and does not need to speak before the vote.
reasons.United States of America: The United States is the penholder and principal sponsor of this draft, which reflects its policy of renewing UNISFA while promoting benchmarks and host-government accountability. It would vote in favour and is likely to speak before the vote to urge adoption.

before.Algeria: Mr. President, Algeria will vote in favour of this resolution. We welcome the inclusion of the African Union and IGAD in the consultation and decision-making considerations, and we appreciate the penholder’s acceptance of our amendments ensuring that any adjustment to UNISFA’s mandate or configuration remains conditions-based and is undertaken in close consultation with the Governments of Sudan and South Sudan, troop- and police-contributing countries, and the African Union and IGAD. The benchmarks must remain indicative and must not become automatic preconditions. We underscore the critical need to protect civilians, ensure full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and uphold the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Sudan and South Sudan. We condemn all attacks against United Nations peacekeepers and call for accountability. Algeria reaffirms its support for UNISFA and for a political solution to the Abyei dispute.
before.China: China supports the renewal of UNISFA’s mandate and commends the mission’s role in stabilizing Abyei and protecting civilians. As a major troop-contributing country, China participated constructively in the consultations. We have consistently maintained that UNISFA’s mandate renewal should not be tied to political benchmarks or used as automatic preconditions. While the revised text offers some clarification, it still retains the benchmark framing and links demonstrable progress by the parties to the Mission’s future. China therefore has reservations and will abstain on this draft resolution. We call on the Council to respect the sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity of Sudan and South Sudan, to take full account of the views of the parties and troop-contributing countries, and to support dialogue and a political settlement on Abyei.
before.France: France votes in favour of this draft resolution. The renewal of UNISFA’s mandate is essential for stabilizing Abyei and protecting civilians at a time when the humanitarian and security situation is deteriorating. We call on Sudan and South Sudan to fully implement their obligations, withdraw unauthorized forces, ensure unhindered humanitarian access, protect United Nations personnel, and engage in good faith in the political process. France also stresses the need for accountability for attacks against peacekeepers and civilians, and supports the benchmarks as incentives for progress rather than automatic preconditions.
before.Greece: Greece will vote in favour of this resolution. We thank the United States for its efforts to bridge positions and reaffirm our full support for UNISFA’s vital stabilization, protection and mediation role in Abyei. We call on Sudan and South Sudan to comply fully with the 2011 Agreement, withdraw all unauthorized forces, keep Abyei demilitarized and weapons-free, and ensure UNISFA’s full and unhindered freedom of movement, including through the timely issuance of visas. Greece condemns all attacks against civilians, humanitarian personnel and United Nations peacekeepers and stresses the need for accountability. We underscore the urgency of safe humanitarian access amid famine risk, the full, equal and meaningful participation of women in peace processes, and the need to consider climate-related security risks. We support the extension of UNISFA’s mandate and a conditions-based approach to its future, while stressing that benchmarks must remain indicative and not become automatic preconditions.
before.Guyana: I have the honour to deliver this statement on behalf of the A3+, namely Algeria, Sierra Leone, Somalia and Guyana. The A3+ has consistently supported UNISFA’s mandate and its essential stabilizing and protection role in Abyei. We therefore vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome that the text confirms the benchmarks in paragraph 2 are indicative and shall not constitute automatic preconditions for the Mission’s renewal, drawdown or adjustment, and that any future decision remains conditions-based and subject to the Council’s determination, in consultation with Sudan, South Sudan, troop- and police-contributing countries, the African Union and IGAD. We also welcome the recognition of the role of the African Union and IGAD. At the same time, we remain gravely concerned by the deteriorating security and humanitarian situation in Abyei and the wider region, including the presence of unauthorized forces, attacks on civilians and peacekeepers, and obstacles to UNISFA’s full deployment and humanitarian access. We call on Sudan and South Sudan to fully comply with the 2011 Agreement, withdraw unauthorized forces, facilitate the deployment of UN police, ensure freedom of movement for United Nations personnel, and engage in good faith toward a political settlement. The A3+ will continue to stand with UNISFA and the people of Abyei.
before.Pakistan: Pakistan will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank the penholder for taking on board the concerns we and others raised, in particular by decoupling the benchmarks from the renewal of UNISFA’s mandate. As a major troop-contributing country, Pakistan reaffirms its full support for UNISFA and for its vital role in protecting civilians, facilitating intercommunal dialogue and maintaining stability in Abyei. We underline the importance of full respect for the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Sudan and South Sudan, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and accountability for all attacks against United Nations peacekeepers.
before.Panama: Panama thanks the United States for its leadership and for accepting our proposal to ensure that the benchmarks in OP2 are reasonable, realistic and developed in close consultation with Sudan, South Sudan, troop- and police-contributing countries and relevant stakeholders. We also welcome the inclusion of language on climate-related security risks and conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence, which are essential to an inclusive and effective mandate. We will vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the extension of UNISFA’s mandate and tasks until 15 November 2026, and we appreciate the United States’ leadership as penholder. The Republic of Korea remains deeply concerned by the continued violence, the presence of unauthorized forces, attacks against peacekeepers, and the deteriorating humanitarian situation in Abyei and the wider region. We underscore the obligations of Sudan and South Sudan to ensure the safety and freedom of movement of United Nations personnel, to allow full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and to comply with the 2011 Agreement and relevant Council resolutions. We also stress the need for accountability for attacks on peacekeepers and civilians. In our view, the benchmarks in this resolution should guide progress by the parties while remaining indicative and not automatic preconditions for the Mission’s renewal or adjustment. The Republic of Korea will continue to support UNISFA’s vital stabilizing role and the protection of civilians in Abyei.
before.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation abstains. We consistently support the continued presence of UNISFA, which plays a stabilizing role in Abyei. However, we cannot support this draft, which retains a flawed premise linking the mission’s renewal to artificial benchmarks and political progress. The penholder has again disregarded the concerns of several Council members, including our red line on OP2, and has inserted extraneous climate-security language. We will not block the extension of UNISFA, but we cannot vote in favour of this unbalanced text.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The renewal of UNISFA’s mandate is essential for the protection of civilians in Abyei, particularly amid the deteriorating humanitarian situation, displacement, famine risk and continued violence. We welcome that the text recognises climate change as a threat multiplier and addresses conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence and the participation of women. At the same time, we stress that benchmarks must remain conditions-based and must not become automatic preconditions that undermine the mission’s ability to protect civilians. We urge Sudan and South Sudan to fully comply with the 2011 Agreement, withdraw unauthorized forces, facilitate UNISFA’s work and ensure accountability for attacks against peacekeepers and civilians.
before.Somalia: Somalia votes in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of UNISFA’s mandate and the Council’s continued attention to Abyei, including the protection of civilians, humanitarian access, and the need for full compliance with the 2011 Agreement. As an African member, Somalia stresses the importance of close coordination with the African Union and IGAD and of ensuring that benchmarks are realistic, conditions-based, and developed in consultation with Sudan, South Sudan, and troop- and police-contributing countries. We call on all parties to withdraw unauthorized forces, protect UN personnel, facilitate humanitarian delivery, and pursue dialogue toward a peaceful resolution of Abyei’s status.
before.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States supports the renewal of UNISFA’s mandate. This resolution preserves the Mission’s vital stabilization and protection role in Abyei while setting clear, realistic benchmarks to encourage Sudan and South Sudan to meet their responsibilities, including withdrawing unauthorized forces, resuming the Joint Political and Security Mechanism and the Abyei Joint Oversight Committee, establishing the Abyei Police Service, facilitating visas for UN police, and supporting a civilian deputy head of mission. The humanitarian and security situation remains grave, and attacks on peacekeepers are unacceptable. We urge Sudan and South Sudan to comply fully with their obligations and call on all Council members to support this draft. The United States will vote in favour.

after.Denmark:
Thank you, Mr. President. Denmark voted in favour of this resolution. We thank the United States for its leadership and for the constructive engagement that allowed the Council to renew UNISFA’s mandate. UNISFA’s protection of civilians role, its support to intercommunal dialogue and its stabilizing presence remain essential for the people of Abyei and for the region. Denmark strongly condemns all attacks against civilians, humanitarian personnel and United Nations peacekeepers. Those responsible must be held accountable.

We remain deeply alarmed by the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Sudan and its impact on Abyei, including the violence in El Fasher, famine in Darfur and South Kordofan, and widespread displacement. We urge Sudan and South Sudan to comply fully with the 2011 Agreement, withdraw unauthorized forces, respect the demilitarized status of Abyei, ensure UNISFA’s full freedom of movement, including timely visa issuance for UN police, and allow full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access.

We welcome the inclusion of language on conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence and on the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women, as well as the recognition of climate-related security risks. The benchmarks in this resolution must remain indicative, realistic and conditions-based, and must not become automatic preconditions. Denmark will continue to support UNISFA and the people of Abyei.
after.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation abstained in the voting on resolution 2802 (2025), on the annual extension of the mandate of the United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei (UNISFA) for another year. We must once again point out the biased approach of the United States penholders of the Abyei file. Despite discrepancies in the text, the penholder decided not to bother seeking a compromise and instead presented a draft in blue that left Security Council delegates with serious questions. While the text was being negotiated, the United States made only cosmetic changes, which did not alter the document’s main message, linking the fate of UNISFA to achievement by the Governments of the Sudan and South Sudan of the benchmarks on resolving the final status of Abyei. We saw no serious changes even after yesterday’s discussions on the text, when there was a risk of the resolution not being adopted at all. The document is based on a flawed premise. The United Nations presence should not hinge on the lack of tangible progress in resolving the situation in this area. Peacekeepers were deployed there precisely to fill the security vacuum and protect civilians from violence. Nevertheless, the Council has adopted a resolution that establishes scenarios for the possible withdrawal of UNISFA for reasons that are not directly related thereto. The authors, knowing full well that virtually all Council delegates, including Russia, have consistently supported maintaining the United Nations presence in Abyei, are trying to set the mission up for failure and to shift responsibility onto the parties. We also note that the draft contains extraneous language on climate and other issues that are not within the mandate of UNISFA. We will not block the extension of the mission, but we cannot vote in favour of this unbalanced text. We call on the penholder to take a more constructive approach and to respect the views of all Council members.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Thank you, Mr. President. The United Kingdom voted in favour of this resolution and welcomes its adoption. We thank the United States for its leadership as penholder and all Council members for their constructive engagement.

UNISFA remains essential to stability and civilian protection in Abyei, and we welcome the extension of its mandate and tasks until 15 November 2026. We urge the Governments of Sudan and South Sudan to comply fully with the 2011 Agreement and with this resolution: withdraw unauthorized forces, keep Abyei demilitarised and weapons-free, ensure UNISFA’s full, safe and unhindered freedom of movement—including timely visas for UN police—and resume the Joint Political and Security Mechanism and the Abyei Joint Oversight Committee without further delay.

The humanitarian and security situation remains grave, and we condemn all attacks on civilians, humanitarian personnel and United Nations peacekeepers. Those responsible must be held to account, and the UNISFA trucks and fuel seized in February must be returned immediately. We also underline the importance of full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access and of the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women in peace processes. We welcome the inclusion of language on conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence and on climate-related security risks, which are central to addressing the drivers of instability in Abyei. The United Kingdom will continue to support UNISFA and the people of Abyei.
after.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States welcomes the adoption of this resolution renewing the mandate of the United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei. We thank Council members for their constructive engagement and for supporting a text that preserves UNISFA’s vital stabilization and protection role while setting clear benchmarks for Sudan and South Sudan to meet their responsibilities. Those benchmarks—withdrawing unauthorized forces and demilitarizing Abyei, resuming the Joint Political and Security Mechanism and the Abyei Joint Oversight Committee, establishing the Abyei Police Service, facilitating visas for UN police, and supporting a civilian deputy head of mission—are intended to encourage measurable progress and accountability. They remain conditions-based and are not automatic preconditions. The security and humanitarian situation in Abyei remains grave. We condemn attacks on peacekeepers and civilians, and we call on Sudan and South Sudan to comply fully with the 2011 Agreement, ensure UNISFA’s freedom of movement, provide full, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access, and pursue a peaceful resolution of Abyei’s status. The United States remains steadfast in its support for UNISFA and for the people of Abyei.
